walkthroughs.body_html:
Tectonic Processes & Hazards — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Tectonic Processes & Hazards brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Tectonic Processes & Hazards.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What was the Tohoku earthquake magnitude?

options: It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Longshore drift carries sediment past a change in coastline direction (e.g. river mouth); deposition continues into deeper water, building a curved depositional landform with a hook.
A spit is a small island just off the coast.
A spit forms where the river deposits its sediment at the coast.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a megacity and a world city?
options: A megacity is defined by population (over 10 million); a world city is defined by global economic and cultural influence (e.g. New York, London) — so a city can be one without the other.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
Megacities and world cities are the same thing.
A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
It is only water evaporating from puddles and lakes.
A spit is a small island just off the coast.
The combined loss of water from a surface through evaporation (from soil and water bodies) and transpiration (from plant leaves).
